_comment: Cycle P (research/tape/cycles.md, 2026-09-13, Fable's ruling): the 2026-09-05 baseline (book_id 2c39ced2697c26cc) could not be reproduced even after pinning the window explicitly (backtest_2y.py --start 2024-09-04 --end 2026-09-04) -- the archive had backfilled INSIDE the pinned window since the 2026-09-05 build (PLTR/QQQ/SPY/CRM/AMZN gained 2026-08-12, 08-13, 08-24, 08-25 that AAPL and the original build still lack), widening it from 499 to 501 distinct sessions and the book from 769 to 770 trades. Per the ruling: the archive is now FROZEN as of 2026-09-13 (research/tape/archive_manifest_2026-09-13.json -- every symbol's first/last session, count and a content hash; backtest_2y.py --manifest that path refuses to run on any further drift unless --allow-drift), backtest_2y.py never writes into data_archive during a rebuild (ARCHIVE_READONLY=1, set unconditionally by backtest_2y.py's own main()) and neither does research/daily_fetch.py while research/tape/.rebuild_lock is held. The loop's ACTIVE baseline is now baseline_2026-09-13 (book_id d5ba41a41d65e1e4, commit 03ffa90a) -- economically identical to the old one (per_day -52 -> -52, mean_r -0.0335 -> -0.0335, 11/25 -> 11/25 green, both halves unchanged to the dollar) but reproducible going forward because the archive under it no longer moves silently. The old 2026-09-05 baseline stays below as baseline_2026-09-05 / baseline_figures_2026-09-05 -- never delete a superseded baseline, same rule as a mark file. research/g212_trace.py's assertions now correctly FAIL: they trace the 2026-09-05 verdict specifically (rebuild.args == ['--days','730'], baseline_book == baseline_2026-09-05.json.gz) and were never updated to the new one -- that is expected, not a regression, see its own docstring note. research/p_pin_trace.py reads book_id and the loop's own unit/slice off any book path, imported from research/loop_cycle rather than re-derived, and is how both baselines above were read.
